name: Black Family Visual Arts Center (Dartmouth)
watch: Leon and Debra Black gave $48 million toward the arts centre, which opened in 2012. Epstein had been a director of the Black Family Foundation, through which the gifts passed; he is still listed on its 2012 tax forms, which the Blacks call an error, saying he left in 2007.
why_flagged: Leon and Debra Black gave $48 million toward the centre, which opened in 2012, through the Black Family Foundation. Dartmouth says it has no current financial relationship with Leon Black.
records_note: No records of its own: parent Dartmouth posts audited financial statements for 2002 to 2025 and names its 25 trustees; no annual report found.
other_findings: Epstein link · Leon Black · documented: Black paid Epstein $158 million to $170 million from 2012 to 2017 and denies knowing of Epstein's crimes. The centre has not been renamed. In June 2026, after community calls to rename it, the trustees set up an ad hoc naming committee.

name: Bard College
watch: Leon Botstein, Bard's president from 1975 to 2026, pursued Epstein as a donor from 2012 to 2019, and Epstein gave to Bard through his foundation Enhanced Education in 2011 and 2012. Epstein attended concerts at Bard's Fisher Center.
why_flagged: Open Society Foundations gave $500M in 2021 to start a $1B endowment campaign, now complete. Epstein's Enhanced Education gave to Bard High School Early College in 2011 and 2012.
records_note: bard.edu has no annual report or financial statements; ProPublica holds Form 990s and audits, a 2018-19 gifts report names donors, and 36 trustees are listed.
other_findings: Epstein link · Leon Botstein · documented: In 2016 Epstein's foundation Gratitude America paid Botstein a $150,000 consulting fee, which he says he passed on to Bard, and WilmerHale found he visited Epstein's townhouse about 25 times and his island for two days between 2012 and 2019. A WilmerHale review commissioned by Bard's trustees found Botstein knew of Epstein's crimes in 2012, did not tell Bard the gifts came from Epstein, and "minimized and was not fully accurate" about the relationship; it found nothing illegal. On 1 May 2026 Botstein announced he would retire as president at the end of June 2026. | Epstein link · Leon Black · documented: Bard president Leon Botstein flew with Leon Black and his wife on their plane to the Virgin Islands, where the Blacks hosted a fundraising dinner on their boat with Epstein present; Bard dates the trip to 2012, and University World News to December 2018. Botstein says the trip led to a $250,000 gift from Black for the arts at Bard about 18 months later. Black paid Epstein $158 million from 2012 to 2017, according to a 2021 Dechert review for Apollo.

name: Djerassi Resident Artists Program
watch: Alexander Maxwell Djerassi has been a Djerassi trustee since 2017 and is now board secretary. An itinerary in the DOJ files lists him and fellow trustee Michael Molesky as guests at a "Mindshift Conference" on the weekend of 7 January 2011, with events on St. Thomas and on Epstein's island, Little St. James.
records_note: Djerassi posts audit reports and Form 990s for fiscal 2014 to 2022 and names its trustees, but no annual report or donor list.
other_findings: Epstein link · Alexander Maxwell Djerassi · documented: He is Ghislaine Maxwell's nephew, and he says of the 2011 lunch, speaking for himself and Molesky, "We had no awareness of Epstein's heinous crimes." Both men remain on the board. The residency calls the 2011 visit a "social lunch" years before they joined the board and says it had no ties to Epstein or Maxwell.

name: MIT Media Lab
watch: MIT's Goodwin Procter review (January 2020) found Epstein gave MIT $850,000 in 10 gifts from 2002 to 2017, nine of them after his 2008 conviction, including $525,000 to the Media Lab under director Joi Ito. The New Yorker reported that Epstein arranged at least $7.5 million in donations to the Lab and that the Lab logged his gifts as anonymous, while MIT's donor database marked him "disqualified".
why_flagged: Funded by member companies. Fourteen joined in 2024, including Sony, HP, Kenvue, Kohler and MITRE.
records_note: The Lab posts annual reports from 2004 to 2025; parent MIT's Form 990s and audits are public, and the MIT Corporation is listed by name.
other_findings: Epstein link · Joi Ito · documented: Ito solicited and accepted Epstein's post-conviction gifts to the Media Lab and hosted his visits, and he also took $1.2 million from Epstein for his own investment funds. Ito resigned on 7 September 2019. MIT committed $850,000 to survivor charities and put Seth Lloyd on paid leave. | Epstein link · Bill Gates · denied: Joi Ito wrote in an email that a $2 million gift from Bill Gates to the Media Lab was "directed by Jeffrey Epstein", while MIT's gift record said only that Gates gave on the recommendation of a friend who wished to remain anonymous. Gates's spokesperson says any claim that Epstein directed his grantmaking is "completely false". Gates met Epstein at least once to discuss philanthropy, and media reports of flight records allege he flew on Epstein's jet from New Jersey to Palm Beach in March 2013. | Epstein link · Reid Hoffman · documented: Reid Hoffman met Epstein at the MIT Media Lab in July 2013, and in 2014 he went to Epstein's island for a fundraising event that Joi Ito says he requested. Their last known in-person meeting was a 2015 dinner Hoffman hosted, and Epstein emailed him in 2017. Hoffman says he dealt with Epstein only for Media Lab fundraising. Hoffman apologised in September 2019 for having "helped to repair his reputation".

name: Poetry in America (Harvard)
watch: Epstein's foundation Gratitude America gave $110,000 in 2016 to Verse Video Education, the nonprofit behind Elisa New's Poetry in America, and New and Epstein emailed about funding her projects from 2013 to at least 2018, including a possible $500,000 donation. Harvard gave the nonprofit office space and paid part of its staff salaries.
why_flagged: Nonprofit Verse Video Education runs it. Elisa New credits the National Endowment for the Humanities and Sloan Foundation for four seasons. Harvard gave office space and part of staff pay.
records_note: The producer, Verse Video Education, posts no reports, funders or board on its site; its Form 990s are on ProPublica.
other_findings: Epstein link · Elisa New · documented: New, a former Harvard professor married to Larry Summers, told the Boston Globe she did not know about Harvard's 2008 ban on Epstein gifts when she took the 2016 donation. GBH ended its ties with the show in 2023, and PBS stopped distributing it in December 2025. Harvard opened an investigation into New and Summers. | Epstein link · Leon Black · documented: Emails released in November 2025 show Epstein brokered a donation of an unspecified amount from Leon Black to Elisa New, which Harvard did not disclose. New wrote to Epstein in 2015 that "The Leon Black gift changed everything for me last year", tying it to her Poetry in America project. Black paid Epstein $158 million from 2012 to 2017, according to a 2021 Dechert review for Apollo. PBS stopped distributing Poetry in America in December 2025.

name: Hasty Pudding Theatricals
watch: The Jeffrey Epstein Virgin Islands Foundation and Gratitude America gave the Hasty Pudding Institute of 1770, the umbrella group for Hasty Pudding Theatricals, at least $375,000: $75,000 in 2013 and $50,000 a year from 2014 to 2019. The Pudding listed Epstein as a 2018 "Guardian of the Sphinx" donor.
why_flagged: Run by the nonprofit Hasty Pudding Institute of 1770. Its 2021 donor list, the latest posted, is led by the Ann and Andrew Tisch Foundation at $50,000 or more.
records_note: Its site posts a 2021 donor list but no reports or board; Form 990s are on ProPublica under the parent club.
other_findings: Epstein link · Jeffrey Epstein · documented: In 2019 members petitioned the board to give the money to anti-trafficking groups. The Pudding removed Epstein's name from its donor page and gave $50,000 to an anti-trafficking nonprofit. Chairman Andrew Farkas says Epstein had no tie to the Pudding beyond giving money.

name: Institut du monde arabe
watch: Jack Lang led the Institut du monde arabe from 2013. He is named 673 times in the DOJ files released on 30 January 2026, and emails show he travelled in Epstein's jet and car.
why_flagged: The French foreign ministry funds over half its income; the founding Arab states stopped paying their share. The TotalEnergies Foundation is its major sponsor, with exhibitions in 2023 to 2025.
records_note: It posts activity reports for 2014 to 2025 (with gaps) and names patrons for 2026, but no accounts or board; only the president is named.
other_findings: Epstein link · Jack Lang · documented: Lang, a former French culture minister, was introduced to Epstein by Woody Allen, called him "a generous sponsor" and exchanged messages with him from 2012 to 2019. Lang resigned as president on 7 February 2026. The day before, the Paris prosecutor had opened a preliminary investigation into him and his daughter Caroline for laundering of aggravated tax fraud. Both deny wrongdoing.

name: Séries Mania
watch: Caroline Lang held roles at Séries Mania, the Lille TV-series festival. La Voix du Nord first reported that she had to give them up after the US Justice Department released Epstein's emails.
why_flagged: Crédit Mutuel Nord Europe has been Grand Partenaire since the festival came to Lille in 2018, renewed in March 2026. No full funder list found.
records_note: The festival's site posts no annual report, accounts or board; partners appear only as logos in the footer, and the team page names directors.
other_findings: Epstein link · Caroline Lang · documented: She held 50% of Prytanee LLC, a company created with Epstein in the US Virgin Islands in 2016, a will Epstein signed promised her $5 million, and she says Woody Allen introduced her to Epstein in 2012. She stood down on 4 February 2026, the same day she left Pictanovo. She calls Epstein an acquaintance and says she received no money or benefit.

name: Pictanovo
watch: Caroline Lang presided over Pictanovo's economic support fund for films and series until 4 February 2026. Pictanovo is an association funded by the Hauts-de-France region.
why_flagged: Regional film agency run as an association. Its economic support fund is paid by the Hauts-de-France region, and public aid is capped at 50% of a work's cost.
records_note: Its site lists the 24-member board in a March 2026 PDF but posts no activity report or accounts; funders show only as logos.
other_findings: Epstein link · Caroline Lang · documented: She co-owned Prytanee LLC, a US Virgin Islands company created in 2016, with Epstein, and an Epstein will document names her for $5 million. She stepped down on 4 February 2026 after the US Justice Department released the Epstein emails. France's National Financial Prosecutor (PNF) has opened a preliminary inquiry into her and Jack Lang on suspicion of laundering aggravated tax fraud.

name: English National Ballet
watch: Prince Andrew was patron of English National Ballet for 18 years. ENB accepted his resignation "with immediate effect" on 22 November 2019, after his Newsnight interview about Epstein, and some ENB trustees had joined calls for him to go.
why_flagged: Arts Council England supports it as a National Portfolio Organisation. Ballymore is principal building partner and Cunard sponsors productions. Trusts include Garfield Weston and Bloomberg Philanthropies.
records_note: Filed accounts for 2024 and 2025 sit at Companies House; its site names donors by level and 11 trustees but posts no annual report.
other_findings: Epstein link · Prince Andrew (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor) · documented: A longtime friend of Epstein, he was arrested on 19 February 2026 on suspicion of misconduct in public office, over whether he passed confidential trade-envoy reports to Epstein, and has not been charged. His patronage ended in November 2019.

name: Royal Philharmonic Orchestra
watch: Prince Andrew was the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra's patron, and the orchestra thanked him for his support "over the past 15 years". In November 2019 its board decided to "part company with its patron, with immediate effect".
why_flagged: Corporate partners include Northern Trust, dunhill and Chapel Down; trusts include the Linbury Trust, Stavros Niarchos Foundation and D'Oyly Carte. Arts Council England's logo is on its supporter page.
records_note: Accounts for 2023 to 2025 are at Companies House; the site names supporters and 16 directors and trustees but posts no annual report.
other_findings: Epstein link · Prince Andrew (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor) · documented: A longtime friend of Epstein, he lost his royal titles in October 2025 and was arrested on 19 February 2026 on suspicion of misconduct in public office over what the Epstein files disclosed; he has not been charged. His patronage ended in November 2019.

name: Amandus Festival
watch: Crown Princess Mette-Marit had been high patron of the Amandus Festival, a youth film festival in Lillehammer, since 2006.
why_flagged: Youth film festival for ages 13 to 20. Its site lists supporters including the Norwegian Film Institute, Innlandet county, Lillehammer municipality, Sparebankstiftelsen and Fritt Ord.
records_note: The foundation behind it files accounts with the Norwegian register, latest 2025; its site names a seven-member board but shows funders only as logos.
other_findings: Epstein link · Crown Princess Mette-Marit · documented: Emails from 2011 to 2014 in the Epstein files show extensive contact between her and Epstein. On 28 April 2026 the festival's board voted unanimously to end the patronage, saying it had become "mer forstyrrende enn styrkende" (more disturbing than strengthening). She said she understood the decision.
